title: Cache hit-rate recommendations (MVP) — copy draft + templates (internal)
body:
Purpose
- Draft UX copy and reusable templates for the first “Cache hit-rate recommendations” MVP. Internal-facing initially (Console stub + internal weekly report).
- Audience: SRE / Runtime / Platform operators + CS/Support + PMs. Later: customer-facing in Console/Optimize.

Guiding principles (copy tone)
- Be specific about what we observed (metrics + window) and what lever to try next.
- Avoid blame-y language (“Your prompts are bad”). Prefer: “We observed low reuse for this route; common causes are…”
- Make it safe-by-default: recommend canary + rollback path, and flag when advice is conditional.
- Privacy note: do not imply we inspected raw prompts. We use bucketing + hashed/canonicalized features only.

Data disclaimer block (reusable footer)
- “Based on aggregated cache telemetry (no raw prompt logging). Metrics are bucketed by request shape and sampled in high-volume routes. Validate changes in a canary before broad rollout.”
- “Recommendation confidence may drop when workload mix changes (new tenants, new prompt-length distribution, or model rollout).”

Recommendation card: standard structure
Title (short, action-oriented)
- Example: “Enable prefix caching for this route”

Impact statement (one sentence)
- “This route is paying repeated prefill cost; enabling prefix caching may reduce p95 latency and $/request.”

What we observed (metric facts)
- Time window: [last_24h | last_7d]
- Route/model context: [deployment_mode], [region], [model_family], [model_version] (where available)
- Metrics:
  - Prefix cache hit-rate: [prefix_hit_rate_pct]
  - KV cache reuse effectiveness: [kv_reuse_pct] (or “reused tokens / total prefill tokens”)
  - Wasted prefill: [wasted_prefill_pct]
  - Eviction pressure: [eviction_rate], [memory_pressure_pct]
  - Miss reasons (top): [miss_reason_1], [miss_reason_2]

Likely causes (ranked bullets)
- Keep these as “common causes” not definitive.

What to try (concrete next steps)
- Show 1–3 steps max.
- Include an example config snippet.

How to validate (quick checklist)
- Which dashboard panel(s) to watch.
- What success looks like in telemetry.

Caveats
- Conditions under which the change could backfire.

Call to action
- Internal: “Ping #eng-platform-telemetry with the recommendation_id if results look off.”
- Customer-facing later: “Contact support if you need help tuning.”

Template placeholders
- [tenant_display_name] (internal only; do not show publicly unless permissions)
- [route_name]
- [deployment_mode] ∈ Hosted | Dedicated | Private
- [region]
- [model_id] / [model_version]
- [prompt_length_bucket] (e.g., 0–512, 512–2k, 2k–8k, 8k+)
- [confidence] ∈ Low | Medium | High
- [estimated_savings] (optional; only if we can justify)

Severity + confidence language (draft)
- High impact + High confidence: “Strongly recommended”
- High impact + Medium confidence: “Recommended (validate with canary)”
- Medium impact + Low confidence: “Consider investigating”

Below are the initial recommendation templates we expect to ship in MVP (copy draft).

---

1) Enable prefix caching for this route
Title
- Enable prefix caching for [route_name]

Impact
- We observed repeated prefill work with minimal reuse. Enabling prefix caching may reduce wasted prefill and improve cost/latency.

What we observed
- Prefix cache hit-rate: [prefix_hit_rate_pct] (low)
- Wasted prefill: [wasted_prefill_pct] (high)
- Miss reasons: policy_disabled is a top miss reason

Likely causes
- Prefix caching disabled at the route level
- Route uses a model/deployment combination where caching defaults are conservative

What to try
- Enable prefix caching on the route.

Example config (illustrative; field names may differ by environment)
- Gateway/route config:
  - cache.prefix.enabled: true
  - cache.prefix.ttl_seconds: 3600
  - cache.prefix.max_bytes: "4GiB"  (start conservative; see #2 if evicting)

How to validate
- Watch: prefix_hit_rate, wasted_prefill, eviction_rate for [route_name]
- Success: hit-rate increases and wasted_prefill decreases without a sustained eviction spike

Caveats
- If prompts are highly unique (low repetition), enabling caching may increase memory pressure without meaningful savings.
- If the route serves multiple distinct prompt templates, consider prompt canonicalization (template #5) to increase reuse.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

2) Increase prefix cache capacity (reduce evictions)
Title
- Increase prefix cache capacity to reduce evictions on [route_name]

Impact
- Evictions can turn would-be cache hits into misses, increasing prefill cost. Increasing cache capacity may improve hit-rate and reduce wasted prefill.

What we observed
- Prefix hit-rate dropped while eviction_rate and memory_pressure were elevated
- Miss reasons: capacity is a top miss reason

Likely causes
- max_prefix_cache_bytes too low for current workload
- Prompt-length distribution shifted upward (more 2k–8k prompts)

What to try
- Increase cache capacity by [X–Y]% and re-check eviction pressure.

Example
- cache.prefix.max_bytes: "8GiB" (was "4GiB")
- If Dedicated/Private: consider increasing GPU memory headroom reserved for cache (requires runtime config + validation)

How to validate
- Success: eviction_rate decreases; hit-rate increases; no p95/p99 regression from memory pressure

Caveats
- Increasing cache memory can reduce headroom for batching/KV cache and may hurt throughput if pushed too far.
- If memory pressure is already high, consider template #3 (TTL tuning) or template #8 (disable caching for low-reuse routes).

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

3) Tune TTL / eviction policy to match reuse window
Title
- Tune prefix cache TTL for [route_name] to match reuse window

Impact
- If TTL is too short, repeated prompts miss. If TTL is too long, cache fills with low-value entries, increasing eviction of high-value prefixes.

What we observed
- Miss reasons include ttl_expired OR eviction pressure is high with low reuse depth
- Reuse appears concentrated in a short window (e.g., bursts during business hours)

What to try
Option A (TTL too short)
- Increase TTL moderately.
  - cache.prefix.ttl_seconds: 7200 (was 3600)

Option B (TTL too long / low-value entries)
- Decrease TTL to keep the cache “fresh.”
  - cache.prefix.ttl_seconds: 1800 (was 7200)

How to validate
- Watch hit-rate and eviction_rate; compare peak vs off-peak

Caveats
- TTL tuning is workload-specific; changes can look “worse” during a workload transition but improve steady-state.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

4) Reduce version mismatch misses (pin or coordinate model rollouts)
Title
- Reduce cache misses from model version changes on [route_name]

Impact
- Version mismatches prevent reuse even when prompts repeat. Coordinating rollouts or pinning model versions can stabilize cache efficiency.

What we observed
- Miss reasons: version_mismatch is a top miss reason
- Hit-rate dip aligns with model_version changes

What to try
- Pin the route to a stable model_version for [N] days, then roll forward with a canary.
- If using A/B or canary: ensure traffic hashing keeps a user/session on the same version to preserve locality.

Example
- route.model_version: "[model_version_A]" (pin)
- rollout.strategy: canary
- rollout.session_stickiness: enabled

How to validate
- Compare hit-rate per model_version; version_mismatch misses should fall

Caveats
- Pinning can slow adoption of bug fixes. For security patches, prioritize correctness over cache efficiency.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

5) Prompt canonicalization (remove volatile fields from the cache key)
Title
- Canonicalize prompts to increase cache reuse on [route_name]

Impact
- Small prompt differences (timestamps, request IDs, user-specific noise) can prevent cache reuse. Canonicalizing the prompt template often increases hit-rate.

What we observed
- Low reuse even for stable prompt-length buckets
- Miss reasons include hash_mismatch (or we see low reuse depth despite repeated traffic patterns)

What to try
- Identify volatile tokens in the system/developer prompt and remove or relocate them.
- For tool/function schemas: keep schema stable; avoid ordering changes.

Examples (common fixes)
- Remove “Generated at: <timestamp>” lines
- Move user/session identifiers out of the cached prefix
- Sort JSON keys deterministically
- Ensure consistent whitespace / punctuation in prompt templates

Suggested message (internal)
- “We did not inspect raw prompts. This recommendation is based on aggregated mismatch patterns. If you share a redacted template, we can help identify likely volatility.”

How to validate
- Look for increased reuse_depth / reused_tokens in the same prompt-length bucket

Caveats
- Do not canonicalize in a way that changes meaning or removes required context.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

6) Improve routing locality (reduce cross-region/cross-pool misses)
Title
- Increase routing locality to improve cache hit-rate for [route_name]

Impact
- Cache effectiveness depends on repeated requests landing on the same cache domain (region/pool). Cross-region routing can lower hit-rate.

What we observed
- Hit-rate varies significantly by region
- Miss spikes correlate with routing shifts or failovers

What to try
- Prefer same-region routing when latency budget allows.
- For Dedicated: reduce pool fragmentation; keep the route on a stable pool when possible.

Example
- routing.policy: "prefer_local_region"
- routing.fallback: "same_model_variant" (avoid cross-model unless necessary)

How to validate
- Compare hit-rate and wasted_prefill by region before/after; ensure overall reliability SLOs remain healthy

Caveats
- During incidents, reliability overrides cache efficiency; expect temporary hit-rate drops during failover.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

7) Address KV cache pressure (decode-side reuse issues)
Title
- Reduce KV cache pressure to improve reuse effectiveness on [route_name]

Impact
- When KV cache is under pressure, reuse effectiveness drops and latency can increase.

What we observed
- KV cache reuse effectiveness: [kv_reuse_pct] is low OR trending down
- Memory_pressure high during decode; eviction-related signals elevated

What to try (choose one)
- Reduce max_generation_tokens for the route (if acceptable)
- Increase KV cache budget / headroom (Dedicated/Private)
- Reduce concurrency or adjust batching targets to avoid sustained pressure

Example
- route.limits.max_generation_tokens: 512 (was 1024)
- runtime.kv_cache.max_bytes: "[increase]" (Dedicated/Private; requires perf validation)

How to validate
- Look for improvements in kv_reuse_pct and p95/p99

Caveats
- This can trade off output length/quality vs performance. Product approval may be needed.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

8) Disable caching for low-reuse routes (avoid waste)
Title
- Consider disabling prefix caching for low-reuse traffic on [route_name]

Impact
- If reuse is consistently near-zero, caching can increase memory pressure and evictions for other routes.

What we observed
- Prefix hit-rate remains near [0–X]% across multiple days and buckets
- Eviction pressure is high and cache entries show low reuse depth

What to try
- Disable prefix caching for this route OR restrict caching to specific prompt-length buckets (if supported).

Example
- cache.prefix.enabled: false

How to validate
- Ensure no regression in latency/cost for the route; monitor that eviction pressure improves for other routes

Caveats
- Confirm the route isn’t expected to have periodic bursts of repetition (e.g., daily workflows). If it is, consider TTL tuning instead.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

9) Investigate telemetry integrity (possible “false dip”)
Title
- Cache telemetry may be incomplete for [route_name] (verify tags + ingestion)

Impact
- A dashboard showing “zero hits” can be caused by ingestion drops or label filtering. Verifying data integrity prevents incorrect action.

What we observed
- Sudden step-change to near-zero hits without corresponding latency/cost changes
- Gaps in metrics or missing expected labels (e.g., route_name/model_version)

What to try
- Confirm the route/model tags are present end-to-end (gateway → runtime → ingestion).
- Check ingestion cardinality guards / drop counters for cache metrics.

Internal links
- Runbook: cache telemetry pipeline incident runbook
- QA: cache-telemetry-data-quality-qa checklist

Caveats
- Do not change cache policy until telemetry is trusted.

Footer
- [DATA_DISCLAIMER]

---

Copy for list view (Console stub)
- Header: “Recommendations (Cache efficiency)”
- Empty state:
  - “No cache recommendations right now. This can mean (a) cache efficiency looks healthy, or (b) telemetry is still ramping. Try expanding the time window.”
- Per-item chips:
  - “High confidence” / “Canary recommended” / “Telemetry check”
- Filter hint (internal):
  - “Filter by: deployment mode, region, model, route, prompt-length bucket”

Microcopy for ‘Why am I seeing this?’ (tooltip)
- “We generate recommendations from aggregated cache telemetry (hit-rate, eviction pressure, wasted prefill) grouped by route/model/region and request-shape buckets. No raw prompts are stored.”

Microcopy for ‘How do I apply this?’ (tooltip)
- “Most changes are route-level cache settings (enable/disable, TTL, capacity) or rollout/routing settings. Apply changes via route config and validate in a canary.”

Terms we should standardize (draft)
- “Prefix cache hit-rate” (not “prompt cache hit-rate”)
- “KV cache reuse effectiveness” (avoid “KV hit-rate” unless we define it precisely)
- “Wasted prefill” (always define once: prefill tokens that did not contribute to subsequent decode due to misses/evictions)
- “Eviction pressure” (bundle: eviction_rate + memory_pressure)

Open questions (to resolve before externalizing copy)
- Are we comfortable showing miss_reason breakdown customer-facing (capacity/ttl_expired/policy_disabled/hash_mismatch/version_mismatch)? If yes, we need clear definitions and avoid implying we saw prompt content.
- Do we want to present estimated savings ($/1k requests) in MVP? My current take: only internal, only when confidence is High.
- Confirm final config key names for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so examples don’t mislead.

Notes from CS/Support feedback (early)
- Customers respond better to “what to try” than raw hit-rate. Include a simple “validate success” checklist.
- For streaming chat, canonicalization and version/stickiness explanations reduce confusion (avoid long text; link to help center later).
